narrative:
The school’s system has analyzed your academic situation and determined that there’s a **14% chance** you might not pass your final year. While this might seem low, the school has set a threshold—any student with a **10% or higher risk** is required to take extra remedial courses to help ensure success. This isn’t a punishment; it’s a precaution based on patterns seen in students with similar backgrounds.

The decision wasn’t made randomly—it focused on three key factors that stood out in your case. The first is **why you chose this school**. Most students attend because of the course quality or proximity to home, but your main reason was the school’s reputation. While reputation is great, it can sometimes mean students don’t engage as deeply with their studies, which might affect focus.

The second factor is **your past academic performance**. Unlike most students who haven’t failed any classes before, your record is clean—but the system also considers how you’re currently performing. Right now, you’re studying **less than two hours a week**, which is significantly below the average for students on track to pass. This is a strong signal that, without extra support, you might struggle to keep up.

Finally, the system noticed that **your long-term goals**—like wanting to pursue higher education—could be at risk if you don’t adjust your study habits now. Many students who don’t take this seriously early on face bigger challenges later, even if they’re motivated.

You’re not alone in this—many students in your situation have turned things around with focused effort. The remedial courses aren’t about failure; they’re about giving you the tools to succeed. Start by **increasing your study time** and checking in with your teachers for extra guidance. Small changes now can make a big difference.
